subject: Conversation throughput surge — mitigation & timeline
messages:
From: Daniel Sullivan <d.sullivan@finwave.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinWave Support <support@finwave.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime stream slowness observed across multiple sessions

Hi Mateo —

We're seeing a sharp increase in latency on the streaming/chat endpoint (POST /v1/conversations/stream) starting ~08:45 PDT. A subset of sessions are pausing for 6–12s mid-response; others show frequent tiny chunks which makes the playback jittery for our agents. This started immediately after our morning traffic spike (we pushed a marketing campaign at 08:30).

Attached is a short sample of client-side traces and a server-side snippet where we log sequence gaps (sample_stream_log.txt). The affected sessions are concentrated in us-west-2.

Impact: degraded agent experience on 7% of conversations, increased retries from our layer.

Can you confirm whether this aligns with anything on your side or if we should revert a client change? We're happy to provide additional traces.

Thanks —
Daniel Sullivan
CTO, FinWave
D: +1 415-555-0199

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Sullivan <d.sullivan@finwave.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream slowness observed across multiple sessions

Daniel — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs, that was helpful. We're starting a triage now. Quick notes and short-term mitigation we can try immediately from your side: 

- Client retry/backoff: Add an exponential backoff for streaming handshakes (initial 200ms, max 3s) and avoid immediate reconnect storms.
- Fallback to polling: If you can enable the non-streaming /v1/conversations/generate path for heavy sessions for 30–60 minutes, that will avoid stream window pressure while we stabilize.
- Stream chunk size: Reduce your consumer-side streaming_chunk_size to 2–3 tokens (if configurable) to avoid processing queue buildup in playback.

Internally I'm looping in Jordan to run edge and queue diagnostics. We'll provide a targeted action list in the next 30–45 minutes.

Attachment: I recommend grabbing logs_20270502.zip and dropping into the shared Drive link so our infra and your team can view them simultaneously.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Sullivan <d.sullivan@finwave.com>, FinWave Support <support@finwave.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream slowness observed across multiple sessions

Team — quick triage summary from infra: we observed a transient congestion event in the us-west-2 edge cluster that caused queue amplification for sessions with long prefix caches. Root observations: 

- Edge shard ew-12 showed an unusual KV-cache eviction pattern between 08:42–09:05, which increased token-expansion work for a subset of model variants.
- A traffic spike from FinWave coincided with a background rebalancing job; the combination produced >2s median delay for first token in ~8% of requests.

Actions taken (completed):
1) Temporarily patched routing policy to avoid ew-12 for FinWave traffic, draining that shard.
2) Increased dedicated batching workers on the customer-affinity pool (+30%) to reduce per-token queueing.
3) Restarted the edge shard process to clear stale KV indexes.

Near-term customer-facing mitigation we've pushed (please confirm):
- Forced fallback routing for FinWave production traffic to our warmed dedicated pool (should be transparent).
- Reduced model variant to a lower-kv profile (trading some latency for lower memory pressure) for 45 minutes.

Attachments: edge_diag_5591.txt (edge shard diag), SR created: SR-2027-5591.

Next steps (owner):
- Infra (Jordan): monitor for 3 hours, post graphs to Drive.
- Solutions (Mateo): confirm with FinWave whether poll fallback is acceptable for high-load endpoints.
- CS (Marissa): propose goodwill credit for the degradation window.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Sullivan <d.sullivan@finwave.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, FinWave Support <support@finwave.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Conversation throughput surge — mitigation & timeline

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for flagging this and for the quick collaboration yesterday. Summarizing where we landed and next steps: 

What happened (short): a coincident traffic surge + background edge rebalancing led to transient KV cache pressure on a us-west-2 shard. That increased token-generation work for affected sessions and produced intermittent pauses in streaming chunk delivery.

What we did (completed):
- Drained the affected edge shard (ew-12) and restarted the process to remove stale KV indexes.
- Rerouted FinWave production traffic to a warmed dedicated pool and scaled batching capacity by +30%.
- Temporarily switched FinWave traffic to a lower-kv model variant while caches warmed back up.

Customer-visible impact window: 08:42–09:10 PDT on 2027-05-02. We estimate ~7–9% of streaming sessions experienced elevated latency or mid-response pauses.

Short-term recommendations for FinWave (to avoid client-side amplification):
- Keep the polling fallback enabled for high concurrency endpoints during peak campaigns.
- Add conservative reconnect jitter and exponential backoff (200ms initial, cap 3s).
- If possible, pin shorter prompt prefixes for high-throughput flows to reduce KV pressure.

Longer-term actions we are pursuing (owner: Infra/Platform):
- Harden the rebalancing window: avoid rebalances during customer peak windows or add pre-warm steps.
- Improve edge shard KV monitoring and set automated preemptive routing when eviction thresholds exceed X%.
- Offer a dedicated reserved pool recommendation for predictable large campaigns; I can share an estimated capacity plan.

Goodwill & follow-up: Marissa will reach out with a proposed credit for the impact window (initial suggestion: 10% of May usage for affected routes). We opened SR-2027-5591 and uploaded full traces to the shared Drive link.

If you'd like, let's schedule a 30-minute postmortem call this week to walk through the graphs and any questions. Proposed slots: Wed 5/5 (09:00 PDT) or Thu 5/6 (14:00 PDT).

Thanks again for your patience — we'll follow up with the postmortem notes and the set of product-side mitigations once they're implemented.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
